name: Task
description: One thing an agent was sent to do with this world, said out loud before it is done. A task is the world's own bookkeeping, not a fact about the person: it is how the world knows where one piece of work starts and stops, which is something it cannot otherwise see — a session key comes from the host's connection settings and outlives any conversation. A task is opened with the start_task tool, worked through over several runs, and closed when nothing is left open about what it touched.

attributes.name: stated
attributes.description: What this task is, in the agent's own words, written before the work starts. It is what the world holds the work against afterwards.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: recording — putting something into the world; answering — finding something out of it. A task is one or the other.

attributes.name: touched
attributes.description: The entities this task wrote to or read from, as they turn up.

attributes.name: closed_as
attributes.description: How it ended. done — nothing it touched was left undecided; for_the_user — what remains was handed on deliberately, because only the user can settle it; abandoned — the task could not be done, and why is in a remark on it.
